body.p: In response to the non-final Office Action dated May 14, 2024, Applicant amends claims 1, 5, 6, and 10, cancels claims 8 and 11-20, and adds new claims 21-24. Claim 1 is in independent form. No new matter has been added. Support for the amendments and added claims can be found throughout the specification as originally filed, for example at the Abstract, page 3, lines 9-12, page 4, lines 15-22, page 5, lines 21-22, page 16, lines 4-6, page 17, lines 1-7, and original dependent claims 5, 6 and 8. Claims 1-7, 9-10, and 21-24 are currently pending. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of all pending claims.
Drawings
Figures IA, 18, 19, 20 and 21 have been objected to under 37 CFR 1.84.

Without conceding the merits of these objections, Figures IA, 18, 19, 20, and 21 have been amended by the submitted replacement sheets rendering the objections moot. The replacement sheets for figures 1A, 18, 19, and 20 are provided to increase the size of text and reference numbers and to increase clarity. The replacement sheet for figure 21 is provided to formalize lines.

Additionally, the drawings are objected to under 37 CFR 1.8(p)(5). The specification is amended as indicated in the above Amendments to the Specification. Applicant submits that these rejections are rendered moot by the above amendments.
Furthermore, the drawings are objected to under 37 CFR 1.83(a). Without conceding the merits of the objection, claim 10 has been amended rendering the objection moot.
For at least these reasons, Applicant respectfully requests that the objections to the drawings be withdrawn.
Specification Objections

Applicant has amended the specification as indicated above in the Amendments to the Specification. No new matter has been added. Applicant submits that the objections to the specification are rendered moot by the above indicated amendments to the specification. Applicant respectfully requests that the objections to the specification be withdrawn.
Claim Objections
Claim 5 is objected to due to informalities. Claim 5 has been amended rendering the objection moot. Applicant respectfully requests that the objection to claim 5 be withdrawn.
Claims 1-10 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) as allegedly failing to comply with the enablement requirement.

Without conceding the merits of the rejection, independent claim 1 has been amended to recite in part "one or more remote-controlled multi-rotor drones configured to deliver a set of modular heliostat units" (Emphasis added) which renders the rejection moot. Applicant contends that independent claim 1, as amended, and the corresponding dependent claims 2-7, 9-10, and 21-24 comply with the enablement requirement. For at least the foregoing reasons, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a) be withdrawn.

Claims 1-10 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor regards as the invention.

Independent claim 1 has been amended to recite in part "each of the one or more remote- controlled multi-rotor drones is selected from drones including a battery powered rechargeable vertical take-off and landing craft having a flight duration of between 10-60 minutes, a total travel range of between 1-20 km, and a payload of between 1-100 kg" (Emphasis added).
Additionally, independent claim 1 has been amended to recite in part "a volume of up to 27 m3" (Emphasis added).

Applicant contends that independent claim 1, as amended, and the corresponding dependent claims 2-7, 9-10, and 21-24 comply with 35 U.S.C. § 112(b). For at least the foregoing reasons, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) be withdrawn.
Claims 1, 3, 5-6 and 8-10 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as allegedly being

unpatentable over Schiller, "Could Solar-Powered Drones Deliver Electricity To The Developing World?" https ://www.fastcompany.com/3056336/ could-solar-powered-drones-deliver- electricity-to-the-developing-world, 2016 (hereinafter "Schiller") in view of Sommer, US Patent 4,172,443 (hereinafter "Sommer") and in further view of Hutson, US Patent Application Publication 2016/0121673 (hereinafter "Hutson").

Without conceding the merits of the rejection, Applicant submits that these rejections are rendered moot by the above amendments. Applicant respectfully requests that these rejections be withdrawn and that the currently pending claims 1-7, 9-10, and 21-24 are put in condition for allowance.

Furthermore, the pending claims are patentable over the asserted references because the references, whether taken alone or in combination, do not teach or disclose the features claimed in amended independent claim 1. For example, claim 1 has been amended to recite in part "wherein the each of the set of the modular heliostat units includes a selectively deployable stand structure with an upper portion forming at least a portion of the attachment mating mechanism, wherein the stand structure comprises multiple tube members operably joined together at attachment points with a cross-shaped perch structure at the upper portion that is operably configured for the remote-controlled multi-rotor drones to land on and selectively engage the cross-shaped perch structure to facilitate pick up and drop off of the modular heliostat unit"
(Emphasis added).
The asserted reference Hutson does not teach or disclose this combination of claimed

features. In the rejection of claim 8, the Examiner relies on figure 51 of Hutson regarding a perch structure, however Hutson does not teach or suggest "a cross-shaped perch structure at the upper portion that is operably configured for the remote-controlled multi-rotor drones to land on and selectively engage the cross-shaped perch structure to facilitate pick up and drop off of the modular heliostat unit" as recited by amended claim 1.

The other asserted reference Schiller does not cure the deficiencies of Hutson. The Office Action relies on Schiller, however Schiller does not teach or suggest "a cross-shaped perch structure at the upper portion that is operably configured for the remote-controlled multi-rotor drones to land on and selectively engage the cross-shaped perch structure to facilitate pick up and drop off of the modular heliostat unit" as recited by amended claim 1.
Additionally, the other asserted reference Sommer does not cure the deficiencies of

Hutson. In the rejection of claim 8, the Office Action points to figures 3-4 of Sommer, however Sommer does not teach or suggest "a cross-shaped perch structure at the upper portion that is operably configured for the remote-controlled multi-rotor drones to land on and selectively engage the cross-shaped perch structure to facilitate pick up and drop off of the modular heliostat unit" as recited by amended claim 1.

As indicated above, the asserted references, whether taken alone or in combination, do not teach or disclose Applicant's claimed features. For at least the reasons discussed above, independent claim 1, and the dependent claims 2-7, 9-10, and 21-24 are patentable over the asserted references. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of these rejections.

Applicant respectfully requests prompt consideration and a Notice of Allowance. In the event that no Notice of Allowance will be provided in the next communication, Applicant requests that the Examiner telephone the undersigned attorney (646-746-2405) prior to the next communication so that prosecution on the merits may be expedited.

It is believed that all of the pending claims have been addressed. By responding in the foregoing remarks only to particular positions taken in the action, Applicant does not acquiesce with other positions that have not been explicitly addressed. In addition, Applicant's remarks above should not be understood as implying that no other reasons for patentability exist. Finally, Applicant's decision to amend or cancel any claim should not be understood as implying that Applicant agrees with any positions taken in the action with reference to that claim or other claims, or that Applicant adopts or agrees with any position except as specifically stated in this paper. In particular, by amending a claim, Applicant does not necessarily concede that the claim prior to amendment was unpatentable.
The fees for excess claims and extension of time are being paid with this reply on the
Electronic Filing System. Apply those fees and any other necessary charges or credits to Deposit Account 50-5196, referencing the above attorney docket number.
Respectfully submitted,
